title: Career Roadmap · Pattern Maker
summary: A Pattern Maker converts garment designs into precise templates used to cut fabric and manufacture clothing. These patterns determine the shape, dimensions, fit and construction of each garment component, such as sleeves, collars, bodices, waistbands and pockets.

about.label: Primary sectors
about.text: Apparel manufacturing, fashion design, garment exports, textile production

about.label: Work environment
about.text: Garment factories, sampling rooms, fashion studios, apparel export houses and technical design departments

blocks.text: A Pattern Maker converts garment designs into precise templates used to cut fabric and manufacture clothing. These patterns determine the shape, dimensions, fit and construction of each garment component, such as sleeves, collars, bodices, waistbands and pockets.

Pattern makers work closely with fashion designers, sample machinists, garment technologists and production teams. Their responsibilities include interpreting design specifications, taking measurements, drafting patterns, developing samples, correcting fit issues and preparing patterns for bulk production.
The role combines creativity with mathematical accuracy, spatial understanding, fabric knowledge and garment-construction skills.

blocks.text: Progression depends on garment-construction knowledge, pattern accuracy, fitting expertise, CAD proficiency and experience with production requirements.
The following plan assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt it to the institution's actual course structure.
Year 1
Foundation
Learn garment construction and basic drafting

items.text: Understand body measurements, sizing systems and measurement accuracy.
Learn basic garment terminology, seams, darts, pleats, collars and sleeves.
Study woven and knitted fabrics, grainlines, stretch and fabric behaviour.
Practise drafting basic blocks for bodices, skirts, trousers and sleeves.
Learn pattern symbols, notches, seam allowances and grainline marking.
Develop sewing-machine familiarity and sample garment construction skills.
Understand how fabric drape and ease influence garment fit.

blocks.text: Year 2
Specialisation
Develop fit and production skills

items.text: Learn pattern manipulation, dart transfer, style variations and design interpretation.
Practise drafting shirts, dresses, trousers, skirts and selected outerwear.
Understand fitting sessions, sample evaluation and correction methods.
Learn grading fundamentals across garment sizes.
Study fabric consumption, marker planning and cutting-room requirements.
Practise preparing pattern sets and technical specifications.
Explore CAD tools such as Gerber, Lectra, Optitex or comparable software available at the institution.

blocks.text: Year 3
Job readiness
Prepare patterns for real production workflows

items.text: Develop complete patterns from garment design briefs and measurement charts.
Create prototypes and refine patterns after fit evaluation.
Practise grading, marker preparation and pattern nesting.
Learn digital pattern digitisation, file management and production handoff.
Understand quality standards, sample approvals and version control.
Complete an internship in an apparel factory, export house or pattern room.
Build a portfolio containing pattern drafts, garment samples, fit corrections and technical documentation.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Basic garment block set
Draft a bodice, sleeve, skirt and trouser block using a consistent measurement chart. Include grainlines, notches, labels and seam allowances.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Shirt pattern and sample
Develop a shirt pattern with front and back panels, collar, collar stand, sleeves, cuffs and placket. Sew a prototype and document any fit or construction corrections.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Pattern grading exercise
Grade one base pattern into a selected size range using a supplied grading rule. Check measurements and compare the proportions across sizes.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Marker and fabric utilisation study
Arrange garment pattern pieces on a simulated fabric width. Calculate marker efficiency and compare alternative layouts without violating grain direction or pattern-placement constraints.

blocks.label: Project 5
blocks.text: Fit correction report
Document a prototype's fitting issues, the measurements or construction details responsible, the pattern changes made and the results after a second fitting.

By the end of the B.Voc programme, the student should aim to have:

items.text: Strong knowledge of body measurements, garment construction and fabric behaviour.
The ability to draft basic patterns for shirts, trousers, skirts and bodices.
Experience developing samples and correcting fit issues.
A foundational understanding of pattern grading and marker making.
Practical experience with at least one CAD pattern-making system, if accessible.
A portfolio containing patterns, technical sheets and finished sample garments.
Internship or supervised experience in a pattern room or apparel production environment.
Good accuracy, spatial reasoning, patience and communication skills.

blocks.text: Final recommendation

For a Pattern Maker career, prioritise accurate pattern drafting, garment fit, construction knowledge and practical sample development. Learn CAD tools alongside manual methods, and document how each pattern translates into a finished garment. A portfolio demonstrating correct patterns, thoughtful fit corrections and production-ready documentation is a strong foundation for entry-level apparel roles.
